page_title: Micro-operation cache: a power aware frontend for variable instruction length ISA

sources.entry: Micro-Operation Cache: A Power Aware Frontend for Variable Instruction Length ISA - Introduces the decoded micro-op cache and its power case, the structure both x86 vendors later built.

summary.title: Micro-operation cache: a power aware frontend for variable instruction length ISA
summary.one_liner: You learn how a micro-operation (uop) cache stores pre-decoded basic blocks to cut frontend decode work and save power in variable-length instruction set processors.
takeaways: A uop cache stores basic blocks already decoded into micro-operations, so the fetch unit can supply a whole basic block per cycle.
Caching pre-decoded blocks avoids repeatedly decoding variable-length instructions and simplifies predicting, fetching, rotating and aligning instructions.
Reported results: a moderate-sized uop cache eliminates about 75% of instruction decodes across benchmarks and over 90% in multimedia and high-power tests.
For existing Intel P6 family processors, the paper estimates about 10% full-chip power savings with no performance degradation.
summary.summary: This 2001 ISLPED paper by Solomon, Mendelson, Orenstien, Almog and Ronen introduces the micro-operation cache (UC), a structure meant to reduce processor frontend power and energy without hurting performance. The UC caches basic blocks of instructions pre-decoded into micro-ops and fetches one basic block's worth per cycle. The abstract reports that a moderate-sized UC removes about 75% of instruction decodes on a broad benchmark set, over 90% for multimedia and high-power tests, and could save about 10% of full-chip power on Intel P6 family processors. The page shown is mostly the abstract and section outline; the full text was behind a sign-in wall.
